behavioral_effects: The repository root carries the standard MIT license with the owner as 2026 copyright holder, so making it public grants the intended rights instead of all-rights-reserved.
compatibility_impact: None. The MIT text matches the license already declared in backend/pyproject.toml.
follow_up: After the owner flips visibility to public: enable secret scanning and push protection, add a branch protection rule on main requiring CI OK, and only then consider Dependabot auto-merge.
limitations: GitHub-side hardening (secret scanning, push protection, branch protection with CI OK required) cannot be configured while the repository is private on the Free plan; delivered as a post-flip checklist instead.
reason: backend/pyproject.toml has declared MIT since adoption but no LICENSE file exists at the root; public-without-license is all-rights-reserved, which contradicts the declared intent and blocks license-aware tooling, so the standard MIT text is added with the owner as copyright holder as part of go-public preparation
rollback: git revert the commit; relicensing after publication cannot retract rights granted to prior copies.
security_impact: None from the license itself. Verified as part of this session: the remote is fully clean post-rewrite, and all four GHCR container packages (backend, frontend, docling-mcp, chrome-devtools-mcp) are private and stay private when the repository flips public.
summary: Add the MIT LICENSE ahead of making the repository public
